messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Help with 'distinct' function returning duplicates, two of same, rather than the first distinct
parts:
Hello D-RUG!

This novice needs a bit of direction in discovering why my script using the Tidyverse/Dplyr 'distinct' function is suddenly returning multiple of the same as distinct from each other. I have done some searching on line to no avail, and I have gone back in to my data to see if something is different some how between the duplicates that is invisible, to no avail.

Here is the dealio:
I want a list of all the distinct bird species detected in my surveys. These are noted as SPID (species identified). SPID is a column/variable in my data (see attached snippet)
Here is the code I am using:
Complete_SPID_list_23_July_2019 <- master_table_clean %>%
  distinct(SPID)
In this example:
list_test_snippet <- snippet_of_Kestrels_data %>%
  distinct(SPID)

This is what I get, NOTE that BRCR is line #10, and then again #44. Same with PUFI, line #24 then again line #43. I also note that line #43&44 are slightly shifted left versus all the others in the list, perhaps indicating some underlying, invisible difference? (Line #16 & 53, NOFL, is the third problem). Yet when I go into the raw data there is no difference?

Why is the distinct function noting two of the same as distinct?

Any help is appreciated!
Kestrel

Hello D-RUG!

 

This novice needs a bit of direction in discovering why my script using the Tidyverse/Dplyr 'distinct' function is suddenly returning multiple of the same as distinct from each other. I have done some searching on line to no avail, and I have gone back in to my data to see if something is different some how between the duplicates that is invisible, to no avail.

 

Here is the dealio:

I want a list of all the distinct bird species detected in my surveys. These are noted as SPID (species identified). SPID is a column/variable in my data (see attached snippet)

Here is the code I am using:

Complete_SPID_list_23_July_2019 <- master_table_clean %>%

  distinct(SPID)

In this example:

list_test_snippet <- snippet_of_Kestrels_data %>%
  distinct(SPID)

 

This is what I get, NOTE that BRCR is line #10, and then again #44. Same with PUFI, line #24 then again line #43. I also note that line #43&44 are slightly shifted left versus all the others in the list, perhaps indicating some underlying, invisible difference? (Line #16 & 53, NOFL, is the third problem).
